preamble: Glottalization of b through fusion with an adjacent laryngeal: [b] + [ʕ] or [ʔ] becomes the ejective [pʼ]. Glottalized bilabials are rare in Cushitic, and Sasse (1979) explains Oromo /pʼ/ (spelled ph) as the result of Proto-East Cushitic *b merging with a neighbouring pharyngeal *ʕ or glottal stop *ʔ, while most other East Cushitic languages simply keep b. The change is conditioned and rare: it happens only in words with such a laryngeal next to *b, not as a general sound law.

examples.note: Saho–Afar /-nʕeb-/ 'to hate' keeps b next to the pharyngeal.

sources: Sasse, H.-J. (1979). The Consonant Phonemes of Proto-East-Cushitic (PEC): A First Approximation. Afroasiatic Linguistics 7(1), 1–67.
